svg.text: K6b GANTRY — hanging mast, one roll axis along +X
X behind a contact-free labyrinth, Z on the mast, Y on the arm, a roll wrist with a force-controlled pin chuck.
roll ±200°, 20 Nm, 0–150 rpm · chuck 20–400 N
payload 6 kg at 160 mm · repeatability ±0.3 mm
5 dynamic seals in the splash zone, none drips into a vessel
Side section: pour about the lip, invert a pair in place
dry box: X rails, belt, purge fan

pair hooked at the far side,

svg.text: One roll axis (chuck along +X), X/Y/Z follow:
• pour any vessel about its lip
• invert a pair (pan, tray, rack, tin + stand)
• spit: turn produce past the peeler post
• tip a tool ≤ 70° about its head
• hang ware on edge in the well (90°)
• not possible: yaw in plan (knives come
in X-cut and Y-cut versions)
X axis: no seal, a labyrinth
Four interleaved lips with 2 mm gaps; the purge fan blows air outward, so
steam and aerosol do not get in. A gutter under the slot catches drips.
dry box (slight overpressure)
gutter
hanger to the mast
purge air out

Y band on the top face of the arm, in a 15 mm gutter sloped 3° to the mast;
Z band on the mast's rear face, facing the wall, draining to a cup.

Wrist: roll lip seal and chuck rod seal

g.text: 1/4 Grip: Z and Y bring the chuck to the pot's tang; the pins pass the tang holes, the load pins weigh the pot
2/4 Pour: the wrist rolls about +X while Y and Z move so that the pot turns about its lip — the lip stays still over the tray
3/4 Invert: a hooked pair turns over in place about its own centre — the same one axis, with Y and Z following
4/4 Back to the park height; the arm passes over a lidded 4 L pot on the rear row
